ops.title: Pin Go/Swift agreement on the same-UID floor with a shared cross-language fixture
ops.description:
Split out of task `352f2119` (Swift same-UID floor), whose security defect is **fixed** — `fe4a534`
made the floor unconditional at the type level. This carries forward the one criterion that was not
met, because it is a *divergence-regression guard* rather than part of the fix.

## What is missing

Nothing pins that Go and Swift agree on the floor for identical inputs. Both enforce it today:

- Go treats the same-UID floor as unconditional on every platform.
- Swift: `SocketServer.swift:140` holds a non-optional `serviceOwnerUserID: uid_t`, defaulted to
  `geteuid()`; `:558` is a bare `guard peer.effectiveUserID == serviceOwnerUserID`.

But the agreement is held by two independent implementations and one shared *intention*. The
wire-session-lifecycle contract names a shared cross-language fixture as the thing that pins it, and
**no such fixture exists in the tree** — verified 2026-07-29: there is no `testdata` directory shared
between the Go packages and `Tests/DaemonKitTests/`, and no cross-language fixture under either.

## Why this belongs to Phase 3, not Phase 2

The plan's Phase 3 already carries a `P3 Swift lockstep` row whose verification cell is
*"macos-26 CI; shared golden-bytes fixture"* — Swift moves in the same commits as each wire deletion.
That is the natural home: the fixture is worth building once, against the post-collapse frame set,
rather than twice.

## Shape

A single golden fixture, read by both suites, enumerating peer/owner uid pairs and the expected
verdict. It must be capable of failing: introduce a divergence in one language and watch exactly one
suite go red.

ops.text: One golden fixture is read by BOTH the Go suite and Tests/DaemonKitTests, enumerating peer/owner uid pairs and the expected verdict — not two fixtures that happen to agree
The fixture is capable of failing: introducing a divergence in one language reds exactly one suite, demonstrated
macos-26 CI green, and the Go job green, both reading the same fixture bytes
